To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interface of the Ising model in 3D is a topological fractal with a high density handles.

1) The mean area of the interface of the 3D Isings model near the critical temperature is an almost linear, increasing function of the genus, 2) The interface of 3D Isinger model has a very high density of handles, and 3) The entropy exponent of the interface of 2D Ising model is affected by very strong finite-size effects.
The interface between domains of the Ising model is a fractal surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interface of the Ising model in the three-dimensional cubic lattice.
the analysis of a 3D interface in the Ising model.
the following questions: (a) What is the structure of the interface of the Ising model near criticality? (b) What is the relation between this structure and the fractal dimension of the interface?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fractal structure of the interface is not a consequence of the finite-size effects.
the interface between the domains of opposite magnetisation in the 3D IsING model is a highly non-trivial topological object.
the 3D interface of the Ising model is not a random curve.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interface of 2D Ising model has a fractal structure with a high density and the entropy exponent depends on the fractal dimension.
the interface of the 3D IsING model is a very complex structure.
the interface is a highly complex, topological structure with an almost linear density of handles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a topological description of the interface in terms of handles is more appropriate than the standard description in terms of loops.
the fractal structure of the interfaces is not affected by the presence of handles.
the interface between domains in 3D critical Ising model is not a smooth surface.
